sanskrit: jalasya dhārāṃ vihitāṃ dṛṣṭvā tāṃ pāṇḍavena ha abravīt sa mahābāhus tāta saṃśāmya pāṇḍavaiḥ
english: Seeing that stream of water sent forth by the Pāṇḍava, the mighty-armed one said, my child: "Make peace with the Pāṇḍavas."

sanskrit: praśamād dhi bhavec chāntir madantaṃ yuddham astu ca bhrātṛbhāvena pṛthivīṃ bhuṅkṣva pāṇḍusutaiḥ saha
english: "For from reconciliation peace would come; let this raging war be ended. In brotherhood enjoy the earth together with the sons of Pāṇḍu."

sanskrit: akurvan vacanaṃ tasya nūnaṃ śocati me sutaḥ tad idaṃ samanuprāptaṃ vacanaṃ dīrghadarśinaḥ
english: Surely my son now grieves, having not heeded his words; for now there has come to pass this very utterance of that far-sighted one.

sanskrit: ahaṃ tu nihatāmātyo hataputraś ca saṃjaya dyūtataḥ kṛcchram āpanno lūnapakṣa iva dvijaḥ
english: But I, my counsellors slain and my sons slain, O Saṃjaya, have through the dice-game fallen into misery, like a bird with its wings clipped.

sanskrit: yathā hi śakuniṃ gṛhya chittvā pakṣau ca saṃjaya visarjayanti saṃhṛṣṭāḥ krīḍamānāḥ kumārakāḥ
english: For just as little boys, O Saṃjaya, seizing a bird and clipping its two wings, set it loose in their delight, sporting at play—

sanskrit: chinnapakṣatayā tasya gamanaṃ nopapadyate tathāham api saṃprāpto lūnapakṣa iva dvijaḥ
english: and with its wings cut off no flight is possible for it—so too am I now reduced, like a bird with its wings clipped.

sanskrit: kṣīṇaḥ sarvārthahīnaś ca nirbandhur jñātivarjitaḥ kāṃ diśaṃ pratipatsyāmi dīnaḥ śatruvaśaṃ gataḥ
english: Wasted away, stripped of every aim, without kinsmen, bereft of my relations—to what quarter shall I turn, wretched and fallen into the power of my foes?

sanskrit: duryodhanasya vṛddhyarthaṃ pṛthivīṃ yo 'jayat prabhuḥ sa jitaḥ pāṇḍavaiḥ śūraiḥ samarthair vīryaśālibhiḥ
english: He, the lord who for Duryodhana's increase had conquered the earth, has been vanquished by the Pāṇḍavas—heroes, mighty, abounding in valour.

sanskrit: tasmin hate maheṣvāse karṇe yudhi kirīṭinā ke vīrāḥ paryavartanta tan mamācakṣva saṃjaya
english: When that great archer Karṇa was slain in battle by the Diademed one, which heroes still stood their ground? Tell me that, O Saṃjaya.

sanskrit: kaccin naikaḥ parityaktaḥ pāṇḍavair nihato raṇe uktaṃ tvayā purā vīra yathā vīrā nipātitāḥ
english: Was he not abandoned and alone when the Pāṇḍavas struck him down in battle? You told me before, brave one, how the heroes were laid low.

sanskrit: bhīṣmam apratiyudhyantaṃ śikhaṇḍī sāyakottamaiḥ pātayām āsa samare sarvaśastrabhṛtāṃ varam
english: Bhīṣma, who would not fight back, Śikhaṇḍin felled in battle with his finest shafts—him, the best of all who bear weapons.

sanskrit: tathā draupadinā droṇo nyastasarvāyudho yudhi yuktayogo maheṣvāsaḥ śarair bahubhir ācitaḥ nihataḥ khaḍgam udyamya dhṛṣṭadyumnena saṃjaya
english: So too Droṇa—that great archer who had laid down all his weapons in the fight and was rapt in yoga, pierced with many arrows—was slain by Draupadī's son, by Dhṛṣṭadyumna with upraised sword, O Saṃjaya.

sanskrit: antareṇa hatāv etau chalena ca viśeṣataḥ aśrauṣam aham etad vai bhīṣmadroṇau nipātitau
english: By stealth were these two slain, and above all by trickery—so I have heard, that Bhīṣma and Droṇa were brought down.

sanskrit: bhīṣmadroṇau hi samare na hanyād vajrabhṛt svayam nyāyena yudhyamānau hi tad vai satyaṃ bravīmi te
english: For Bhīṣma and Droṇa, were they fighting by fair means, not even the Wielder of the Thunderbolt himself could slay them in battle—this truth I declare to you.

sanskrit: karṇaṃ tv asyantam astrāṇi divyāni ca bahūni ca katham indropamaṃ vīraṃ mṛtyur yuddhe samaspṛśat
english: But Karṇa, hurling his many celestial weapons—how did death touch in battle that hero who was the equal of Indra?

sanskrit: yasya vidyutprabhāṃ śaktiṃ divyāṃ kanakabhūṣaṇām prāyacchad dviṣatāṃ hantrīṃ kuṇḍalābhyāṃ puraṃdaraḥ
english: He to whom, in exchange for his earrings, Purandara gave that celestial spear, gleaming like lightning and adorned with gold, the slayer of foes—

sanskrit: yasya sarpamukho divyaḥ śaraḥ kanakabhūṣaṇaḥ aśeta nihataḥ patrī candaneṣv arisūdanaḥ
english: he whose celestial serpent-mouthed shaft, gold-adorned and feathered, the destroyer of foes, lay resting amid the sandalwood—

sanskrit: bhīṣmadroṇamukhān vīrān yo 'vamanya mahārathān jāmadagnyān mahāghoraṃ brāhmam astram aśikṣata
english: he who, scorning such heroes and great chariot-warriors as Bhīṣma and Droṇa, learned from the son of Jamadagni the most terrible Brahmā weapon—

sanskrit: yaś ca droṇamukhān dṛṣṭvā vimukhān arditāñ śaraiḥ saubhadrasya mahābāhur vyadhamat kārmukaṃ śaraiḥ
english: he, the mighty-armed, who when he saw Droṇa and the rest turned away and tormented by arrows, shattered with his shafts the bow of Subhadrā's son—

sanskrit: yaś ca nāgāyutaprāṇaṃ vātaraṃhasam acyutam virathaṃ bhrātaraṃ kṛtvā bhīmasenam upāhasat
english: he who, having made my brother's foe Bhīmasena chariotless—him whose strength was that of ten thousand elephants, swift as the wind and unfaltering—laughed at him in mockery—

sanskrit: sahadevaṃ ca nirjitya śaraiḥ saṃnataparvabhiḥ kṛpayā virathaṃ kṛtvā nāhanad dharmavittayā
english: he who, having vanquished Sahadeva with his straight-jointed arrows and left him chariotless, out of compassion and his knowledge of the right did not slay him—

sanskrit: yaś ca māyāsahasrāṇi dhvaṃsayitvā raṇotkaṭam ghaṭotkacaṃ rākṣasendraṃ śakraśaktyābhijaghnivān
english: he who, having scattered a thousand illusions, struck down with Śakra's spear that lord of the Rākṣasas, the battle-frenzied Ghaṭotkaca—

sanskrit: etāni divasāny asya yuddhe bhīto dhanaṃjayaḥ nāgamad dvairathaṃ vīraḥ sa kathaṃ nihato raṇe
english: all these days Dhanaṃjaya, afraid of him in battle, that hero, never came to single combat—how then was he slain in the fight?

sanskrit: rathasaṅgo na cet tasya dhanur vā na vyaśīryata na ced astrāṇi nirṇeśuḥ sa kathaṃ nihataḥ paraiḥ
english: If his chariot was not stuck fast, if his bow did not shatter, if his weapons did not fail him—how then was he slain by the foe?

sanskrit: ko hi śakto raṇe karṇaṃ vidhunvānaṃ mahad dhanuḥ vimuñcantaṃ śarān ghorān divyāny astrāṇi cāhave jetuṃ puruṣaśārdūlaṃ śārdūlam iva vegitam
english: Who indeed was able in battle to conquer Karṇa, that tiger among men—shaking his great bow, loosing his dreadful shafts and celestial weapons in the fray, swift as a tiger in its rush?

sanskrit: dhruvaṃ tasya dhanuś chinnaṃ ratho vāpi gato mahīm astrāṇi vā pranaṣṭāni yathā śaṃsasi me hatam na hy anyad anupaśyāmi kāraṇaṃ tasya nāśane
english: Surely his bow was cut through, or his chariot sank into the earth, or his weapons failed—since you tell me he is slain; for I can see no other cause of his destruction.

sanskrit: na hanyām arjunaṃ yāvat tāvat pādau na dhāvaye iti yasya mahāghoraṃ vratam āsīn mahātmanaḥ
english: "I will not wash my feet until I have slain Arjuna"—such was the most terrible vow of that great-souled one.

sanskrit: yasya bhīto vane nityaṃ dharmarājo yudhiṣṭhiraḥ trayodaśa samā nidrāṃ na lebhe puruṣarṣabhaḥ
english: He of whom Yudhiṣṭhira, the King of Righteousness, that bull among men, was ever afraid in the forest, and for thirteen years could find no sleep—

sanskrit: yasya vīryavato vīryaṃ samāśritya mahātmanaḥ mama putraḥ sabhāṃ bhāryāṃ pāṇḍūnāṃ nītavān balāt
english: he upon whose valour—the valour of that mighty, great-souled one—my son relied when he dragged by force into the assembly the wife of the Pāṇḍavas—

sanskrit: tatra cāpi sabhāmadhye pāṇḍavānāṃ ca paśyatām dāsabhāryeti pāñcālīm abravīt kurusaṃsadi
english: and there too, in the midst of the assembly, before the very eyes of the Pāṇḍavas, called Pāñcālī "a slave's wife" in the gathering of the Kurus—

sanskrit: yaś ca gāṇḍīvamuktānāṃ sparśam ugram acintayan apatir hy asi kṛṣṇeti bruvan pārthān avaikṣata
english: he who, reckoning nothing of the fierce touch of shafts loosed from the Gāṇḍīva, said "Kṛṣṇā, you have now no husband," and gazed upon the sons of Pṛthā—

sanskrit: yasya nāsīd bhayaṃ pārthaiḥ saputraiḥ sajanārdanaiḥ svabāhubalam āśritya muhūrtam api saṃjaya
english: he who, relying on the strength of his own arms, had no fear of the sons of Pṛthā, even for a moment, O Saṃjaya—not though their sons and Janārdana stood with them—

sanskrit: tasya nāhaṃ vadhaṃ manye devair api savāsavaiḥ pratīpam upadhāvadbhiḥ kiṃ punas tāta pāṇḍavaiḥ
english: his slaying I cannot believe possible even by the gods with Vāsava himself rushing against him—how much less, my child, by the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: na hi jyāṃ spṛśamānasya talatre cāpi gṛhṇataḥ pumān ādhiratheḥ kaś cit pramukhe sthātum arhati
english: For when the son of Adhiratha touched his bowstring and took up his leather guard, no man living was fit to stand before him.

sanskrit: api syān medinī hīnā somasūryaprabhāṃśubhiḥ na vadhaḥ puruṣendrasya samareṣv apalāyinaḥ
english: Sooner might the earth be bereft of the radiant beams of moon and sun than that lord of men, who never fled the field, should be slain in battle.

sanskrit: yadi mandaḥ sahāyena bhrātrā duḥśāsanena ca vāsudevasya durbuddhiḥ pratyākhyānam arocayat
english: If that dull-witted fool, with his brother Duḥśāsana for ally, took pleasure in rejecting the counsel of Vāsudeva—

sanskrit: sa nūnam ṛṣabhaskandhaṃ dṛṣṭvā karṇaṃ nipātitam duḥśāsanaṃ ca nihataṃ manye śocati putrakaḥ
english: surely now, beholding bull-shouldered Karṇa struck down and Duḥśāsana slain, my poor son must grieve—so I think.

sanskrit: hataṃ vaikartanaṃ śrutvā dvairathe savyasācinā jayataḥ pāṇḍavān dṛṣṭvā kiṃ svid duryodhano 'bravīt
english: Hearing that Vaikartana was slain in single combat by the Ambidextrous one, and seeing the Pāṇḍavas victorious, what then did Duryodhana say?

sanskrit: durmarṣaṇaṃ hataṃ śrutvā vṛṣasenaṃ ca saṃyuge prabhagnaṃ ca balaṃ dṛṣṭvā vadhyamānaṃ mahārathaiḥ
english: Hearing that Durmarṣaṇa was slain, and Vṛṣasena too in the fight, and seeing his host broken and cut down by the great chariot-warriors—

sanskrit: parāṅmukhāṃs tathā rājñaḥ palāyanaparāyaṇān vidrutān rathino dṛṣṭvā manye śocati putrakaḥ
english: and seeing his kings turned away, bent only on flight, his chariot-warriors scattered in rout—my poor son, I think, must grieve.

sanskrit: aneyaś cābhimānena bālabuddhir amarṣaṇaḥ hatotsāhaṃ balaṃ dṛṣṭvā kiṃ svid duryodhano 'bravīt
english: Unteachable through pride, childish of mind, unforgiving—seeing his host's spirit broken, what then did Duryodhana say?

sanskrit: bhrātaraṃ nihataṃ dṛṣṭvā bhīmasenena saṃyuge rudhiraṃ pīyamānena kiṃ svid duryodhano 'bravīt
english: Seeing his brother slain in the fight by Bhīmasena, who drank his blood—what then did Duryodhana say?

sanskrit: saha gāndhārarājena sabhāyāṃ yad abhāṣata karṇo 'rjunaṃ raṇe hantā hate tasmin kim abravīt
english: "Karṇa shall slay Arjuna in battle"—so he declared in the assembly together with the king of Gāndhāra; now that Karṇa is slain, what did he say?

sanskrit: dyūtaṃ kṛtvā purā hṛṣṭo vañcayitvā ca pāṇḍavān śakuniḥ saubalas tāta hate karṇe kim abravīt
english: Śakuni, the son of Subala, who once played the dice in glee and cheated the Pāṇḍavas—what, my child, did he say when Karṇa was slain?

sanskrit: kṛtavarmā maheṣvāsaḥ sātvatānāṃ mahārathaḥ karṇaṃ vinihataṃ dṛṣṭvā hārdikyaḥ kim abhāṣata
english: Kṛtavarman, that great archer, the mighty chariot-warrior of the Sātvatas, the son of Hṛdika—seeing Karṇa utterly slain, what did he say?

sanskrit: brāhmaṇāḥ kṣatriyā vaiśyā yasya śikṣām upāsate dhanurvedaṃ cikīrṣanto droṇaputrasya dhīmataḥ
english: He at whose instruction Brāhmaṇas, Kṣatriyas, and Vaiśyas wait, longing to master the science of the bow—the wise son of Droṇa—

sanskrit: yuvā rūpeṇa saṃpanno darśanīyo mahāyaśāḥ aśvatthāmā hate karṇe kim abhāṣata saṃjaya
english: that youthful one, endowed with beauty, fair to look upon, of great renown—Aśvatthāman, when Karṇa was slain, what did he say, O Saṃjaya?

sanskrit: ācāryatvaṃ dhanurvede gataḥ paramatattvavit kṛpaḥ śāradvatas tāta hate karṇe kim abravīt
english: Kṛpa, the son of Śaradvat, who had attained mastery in the science of the bow and knew the highest truths—what, my child, did he say when Karṇa was slain?

sanskrit: madrarājo maheṣvāsaḥ śalyaḥ samitiśobhanaḥ diṣṭaṃ tena hi tat sarvaṃ yathā karṇo nipātitaḥ
english: Śalya, the king of the Madras, that great archer, the ornament of assemblies—surely all that was ordained by him, the manner in which Karṇa was brought down.

sanskrit: ye ca ke cana rājānaḥ pṛthivyāṃ yoddhum āgatāḥ vaikartanaṃ hataṃ dṛṣṭvā kim abhāṣanta saṃjaya
english: And whatever kings of the earth had come to do battle—seeing Vaikartana slain, what did they say, O Saṃjaya?

sanskrit: karṇe tu nihate vīre rathavyāghre nararṣabhe kiṃ vo mukham anīkānām āsīt saṃjaya bhāgaśaḥ
english: When the hero Karṇa was slain—that tiger among chariot-warriors, that bull among men—what, O Saṃjaya, became of the front ranks of your several armies?

sanskrit: madrarājaḥ kathaṃ śalyo niyukto rathināṃ varaḥ vaikartanasya sārathye tan mamācakṣva saṃjaya
english: How came Śalya, the king of the Madras, the best of chariot-warriors, to be appointed to the charioteering of Vaikartana? Tell me that, O Saṃjaya.

sanskrit: ke 'rakṣan dakṣiṇaṃ cakraṃ sūtaputrasya saṃyuge vāmaṃ cakraṃ rarakṣur vā ke vā vīrasya pṛṣṭhataḥ
english: Who guarded the right wheel of the Sūta's son in the fight, who the left wheel, and who guarded the hero from behind?

sanskrit: ke karṇaṃ vājahuḥ śūrāḥ ke kṣudrāḥ prādravan bhayāt kathaṃ ca vaḥ sametānāṃ hataḥ karṇo mahārathaḥ
english: Which heroes stood by Karṇa, and which base ones fled in fear? And how, while you were all assembled together, was the great chariot-warrior Karṇa slain?

sanskrit: pāṇḍavāś ca kathaṃ śūrāḥ pratyudīyur mahāratham sṛjantaṃ śaravarṣāṇi vāridhārā ivāmbudam
english: And how did the heroic Pāṇḍavas come on against that great chariot-warrior as he poured forth showers of arrows, like a cloud loosing streams of rain?

sanskrit: sa ca sarpamukho divyo maheṣupravaras tadā vyarthaḥ kathaṃ samabhavat tan mamācakṣva saṃjaya
english: And how did that celestial serpent-mouthed shaft, the choicest of great arrows, then come to naught? Tell me that, O Saṃjaya.

sanskrit: māmakasyāsya sainyasya hṛtotsedhasya saṃjaya avaśeṣaṃ na paśyāmi kakude mṛdite sati
english: Of this my host, its eminence now plucked away, O Saṃjaya, I can see no remnant left, its very crest crushed.

sanskrit: tau hi vīrau maheṣvāsau madarthe kurusattamau bhīṣmadroṇau hatau śrutvā ko nv artho jīvitena me
english: Those two heroes, those great archers, those best of the Kurus—Bhīṣma and Droṇa—slain in my cause: hearing it, what worth has life for me?

sanskrit: na mṛṣyāmi ca rādheyaṃ hatam āhavaśobhinam yasya bāhvor balaṃ tulyaṃ kuñjarāṇāṃ śataṃ śatam
english: And I cannot bear that Rādheya is slain, the ornament of battle, the strength of whose two arms was equal to a hundred hundred elephants.

sanskrit: droṇe hate ca yad vṛttaṃ kauravāṇāṃ paraiḥ saha saṃgrāme naravīrāṇāṃ tan mamācakṣva saṃjaya
english: And what befell the Kauravas, the heroes among men, in their battle with the foe after Droṇa was slain—tell me that, O Saṃjaya.

sanskrit: yathā ca karṇaḥ kaunteyaiḥ saha yuddham ayojayat yathā ca dviṣatāṃ hantā raṇe śāntas tad ucyatām
english: And how Karṇa joined battle with the sons of Kuntī, and how that slayer of foes was stilled in the fight—let that be told.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca hate droṇe maheṣvāse tasminn ahani bhārata kṛte ca moghasaṃkalpe droṇaputre mahārathe
english: Saṃjaya said: When the great archer Droṇa had been slain on that day, O descendant of Bharata, and when the great chariot-warrior, Droṇa's son, had been made vain in his resolve—

sanskrit: dravamāṇe mahārāja kauravāṇāṃ bale tathā vyūhya pārthaḥ svakaṃ sainyam atiṣṭhad bhrātṛbhiḥ saha
english: as the host of the Kauravas streamed away in flight, O great king, the son of Pṛthā drew up his own army in array and stood firm together with his brothers.

sanskrit: tam avasthitam ājñāya putras te bharatarṣabha dravac ca svabalaṃ dṛṣṭvā pauruṣeṇa nyavārayat
english: Knowing him to stand his ground, O bull of the Bhāratas, and seeing his own force in flight, your son by his manly might held it back.

sanskrit: svam anīkam avasthāpya bāhuvīrye vyavasthitaḥ yuddhvā ca suciraṃ kālaṃ pāṇḍavaiḥ saha bhārata
english: Having steadied his own ranks and taken his stand upon the strength of his arms, he fought for a long while with the Pāṇḍavas, O descendant of Bharata—

sanskrit: labdhalakṣaiḥ parair hṛṣṭair vyāyacchadbhiś ciraṃ tadā saṃdhyākālaṃ samāsādya pratyāhāram akārayat
english: with foes who had found their mark, exultant, long striving against him; and then, as the hour of twilight came on, he ordered the withdrawal.

sanskrit: kṛtvāvahāraṃ sainyānāṃ praviśya śibiraṃ svakam kuravo ''tmahitaṃ mantraṃ mantrayāṃ cakrire tadā
english: Having drawn back their forces and entered their own camp, the Kurus then took counsel together for their own welfare.

sanskrit: paryaṅkeṣu parārdhyeṣu spardhyāstaraṇavatsu ca varāsaneṣūpaviṣṭāḥ sukhaśayyāsv ivāmarāḥ
english: Seated upon priceless couches spread with coverings beyond compare, upon excellent seats, they were like the immortals upon their pleasant beds.

sanskrit: tato duryodhano rājā sāmnā paramavalgunā tān ābhāṣya maheṣvāsān prāptakālam abhāṣata
english: Then King Duryodhana, addressing those great archers with words most winning and gentle, spoke what the moment called for:

sanskrit: matiṃ matimatāṃ śreṣṭhāḥ sarve prabrūta māciram evaṃ gate tu yat kāryaṃ bhavet kāryakaraṃ nṛpāḥ
english: "You best of the wise, declare your counsel, all of you, without delay—what task, things being thus, would best serve our purpose, O kings."

sanskrit: evam ukte narendreṇa narasiṃhā yuyutsavaḥ cakrur nānāvidhāś ceṣṭāḥ siṃhāsanagatās tadā
english: When the lord of men had thus spoken, those lions among men, eager for the fight, then made gestures of many kinds, seated upon their lion-thrones.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ niśamyeṅgitāni yuddhe prāṇāñ juhūṣatām samudvīkṣya mukhaṃ rājño bālārkasamavarcasaḥ ācāryaputro medhāvī vākyajño vākyam ādade
english: Marking the bearing of those who longed to offer up their lives in battle, and gazing upon the face of the king, whose splendour was like the rising sun, the Preceptor's son, wise and skilled in speech, took up the word:

sanskrit: rāgo yogas tathā dākṣyaṃ nayaś cety arthasādhakāḥ upāyāḥ paṇḍitaiḥ proktāḥ sarve daivasamāśritāḥ
english: "Zeal, application, skill, and good policy—these means of achieving an end have been named by the learned; yet all of them rest upon fate."

sanskrit: lokapravīrā ye 'smākaṃ devakalpā mahārathāḥ nītimantas tathā yuktā dakṣā raktāś ca te hatāḥ
english: "Those foremost heroes of the world among us, the godlike great chariot-warriors, prudent, disciplined, skilled, and devoted—they have been slain."

sanskrit: na tv eva kāryaṃ nairāśyam asmābhir vijayaṃ prati sunītair iha sarvārthair daivam apy anulomyate
english: "Yet we must not despair of victory; by sound policy in all our undertakings even fate may be turned to favour."

sanskrit: te vayaṃ pravaraṃ nṝṇāṃ sarvair guṇagaṇair yutam karṇaṃ senāpatiṃ kṛtvā pramathiṣyāmahe ripūn
english: "So let us make Karṇa, the foremost of men, endowed with every host of virtues, our commander, and crush the foe."

sanskrit: tato duryodhanaḥ prītaḥ priyaṃ śrutvā vacas tadā prītisaṃskārasaṃyuktaṃ tathyam ātmahitaṃ śubham
english: Then Duryodhana, delighted to hear that pleasing speech—charged with the grace of affection, true, salutary, and auspicious to himself—

sanskrit: svaṃ manaḥ samavasthāpya bāhuvīryam upāśritaḥ duryodhano mahārāja rādheyam idam abravīt
english: having steadied his mind and leaning upon the strength of his arms, Duryodhana, O great king, said this to Rādheya:

sanskrit: karṇa jānāmi te vīryaṃ sauhṛdaṃ ca paraṃ mayi tathāpi tvāṃ mahābāho pravakṣyāmi hitaṃ vacaḥ
english: "Karṇa, I know your valour and your supreme love for me; yet even so, mighty-armed one, I shall speak to you a word for your good."

sanskrit: śrutvā yatheṣṭaṃ ca kuru vīra yat tava rocate bhavān prājñatamo nityaṃ mama caiva parā gatiḥ
english: "Having heard it, do then as you will, brave one, whatever pleases you; for you are ever the wisest of all, and my supreme refuge."
